 Trial by fire: Senate bureau apologizes for video glitch
 Marc Jayson Cayabyab - The Philippine Star November 20, 2026 | 12:00am 
 Defense lawyer Mark Vinluan presents a video clip of the late chief justice Renato Corona’s impeachment trial, during Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial at the Senate on November 20, 2026. Noel Pabalate 
 MANILA, Philippines — A glitch in the livestream literally turned the Senate impeachment court proceedings into a trial by fire.
 The Senate Public Relations and Information Bureau (PRIB) apologized for the “technical issue” that saw a fire transition during the prayer being delivered by Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano.
 “We sincerely apologize for the accidental transition effect that appeared during the livestream of the Senate Impeachment Court proceedings today. The incident was due to an unexpected technical issue during the broadcast, which we deeply regret,” the PRIB said in a statement.
 “The PRIB is currently upgrading its equipment and undergoing retraining and upskilling of its technical staff in a bid to strengthen the quality of broadcast media coverage for the Filipino people,” it added.
 The viral incident has reached the attention of the court, prompting presiding officer Francis Escudero when the trial resumed after lunch break to order the Clerk of Court to take down the video.
 “Kindly instruct the PRIB to be more mindful and respectful of the transition effects,” Escudero said in extinguishing the frenzy caused by the fire transition.
 “The flames are not well taken and are inappropriate for this proceeding. So kindly be mindful. The Clerk of Court is ordered to remove and edit it from the record of the Impeachment Court, as it is deemed inappropriate,” he added.
 The livestream of the trial was taken down after the court adjourned past 5 p.m., but too late for the court to prevent being feasted on with memes on social media.
 While netizens in the comment section laughed at the coincidence of having what looked like “hell flames” appear during Cayetano’s prayer, others said the transition could also be seen as the “Holy Fire of God.”
